_about: The season cycle as data (user, 2031-05-28: workflows defined at the top level, so every loop runs every step). `fm cycle` goes to the next checkpoint and runs it: inside a transfer window it drives the game with the autopilot (bids, loan offers, deadline deals; a match day is a one-day holiday so the assistant plays it), outside the windows it holidays (user, 2031-08-08); `fm checkpoint <name>` runs one now. Each step is a capability function (capabilities/season/checkpoint.mjs STEPS) that writes one section of the report in local/reports/checkpoints/. Steps run in code, in order: none depends on the model remembering it. Decisions start after the report. Why each checkpoint exists: PLAYBOOK §1b.

checkpoints.name: january
checkpoints.why: Contracts ending in June: ours (renew or sell) and everyone else's (pre-contracts: free players, the cheapest Moneyball signing). Then the wonderkid portfolio (user, 2031-08-08: the free agents and the wonderkids were the best buys).

checkpoints.name: newgen
checkpoints.why: 95% of the youth intakes land in March-April: shortlist the new class. Free agents too (user, 2026-10-18: Rusnák and Holmbjerg were missed): every free or expiring player we'd want gets a verdict.

checkpoints.name: season_end
checkpoints.why: After the last league match: the season's scoreboard. Players at English clubs whose contracts end in June become approachable now (no in-season pre-contract between English clubs): the watch list first (Monga, Burton, user 2032-01-01). Bid now (user, 2035-06-18: Wark, Baldé and Quenda were gone by 2 July; FM accepts bids while the window is closed): the buy and sell tables run here, every target gets its bid today, and the summer checkpoint is the second pass with full-season stats.

checkpoints.name: summer
checkpoints.why: After the rollover, before the first league match: the only time the export has full-season stats. The window's plan.
